correctness.rationale: Both kernels are Π plus half an orthogonal rank-one projection onto a unit zero-sum mode (adjacent difference u or endpoint difference w); positivity, uniform stationarity, spectrum, gap and half the maximum row ℓ¹ distance follow. The Gaussian Gram kernel is strictly positive definite (its Fourier density is everywhere positive and the trigonometric polynomial of a nonzero coefficient vector is not identically zero). Every zero-mass direction is realized by a sufficiently small probability perturbation of π, so the computed gain is sharp over probability laws. Independently, the zero-mass reflection basis w,(1,−2,1)/√6 yields diagonal metric entries λ₁=1−t⁴, λ₂=(1−t)²(t²+2t+3)/3. The endpoint projection is metric-orthogonal. The adjacent mode has squared basis coordinates 1/4 and 3/4; by Cauchy–Schwarz in the metric, its gain squared is ((λ₁+3λ₂)/4)((1/λ₁+3/λ₂)/4)/4, which simplifies to the claimed 1/[4(1−R)]. For A=t+t²+t³, R=A²/(3+2A), strictly increasing from 0 to 1. R=3/4 gives the polynomial and unique transition with the stated direction. From λ₁∼4h and λ₂∼2h² the sharp adjacent gain squared is asymptotic to 3/(32h). On two states the zero-mass subspace is one-dimensional, so kernel choice cannot change the ratio at fixed eigenvalue. h=0 is excluded and no indefinite trajectory growth is implied.
